rationale: Data engineers at Salesforce Data Cloud shops are losing real engineering hours to invisible encoding bugs — companies paying enterprise Salesforce licenses ($150k+/yr) will spend $50–$200/mo on a tool that reliably pre-validates and auto-fixes CSV encoding before SFTP ingestion. The buyer is a specific, named role (Salesforce Data Cloud admin / data engineer) at identifiable mid-market to enterprise companies, and they have budget authority for tooling at this price point. The build is feasible — a Claude-powered CSV pre-flight checker (detect BOM, encoding, special characters) with a simple upload UI and a Stripe subscription is shippable quickly. It misses the build threshold (6.4 vs 6.5 required) and responsiveness is untested, so validate first: reach out to Salesforce Data Cloud communities (Trailblazer, Stack Exchange, LinkedIn) to confirm willingness to pay before building.
solution_plan: The micro-service is a CSV pre-flight validator and auto-fixer for Salesforce Data Cloud SFTP ingestion: users upload a CSV, Claude detects UTF-8 BOM, Windows-1252 artifacts, invalid column names, and other known ingestion-killers, then returns a clean file and a report. BUILD: the factory creates a simple upload form (no-code page), a Claude prompt that runs the encoding checks and produces a cleaned CSV + a plain-English report, and a Stripe subscription link ($49–$99/mo per pipeline). No operator coding required. SELL: target Salesforce Data Cloud admins and data engineers via Salesforce Trailblazer Community posts, LinkedIn outreach to 'Salesforce Data Cloud' job-title holders, and answers on Salesforce Stack Exchange — outreach batches go out only after Youval approves them. MAINTAIN: file uploads trigger Claude automatically, cleaned files and reports are returned by email or download link, billing runs via Stripe, and support questions are handled by a Claude-powered inbox; the only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and reviewing the weekly revenue summary.
notes: Total is 6.4, just below the 6.5 build gate threshold, so validate stage is correct regardless. All build_gates would be met if validated (operational_autonomy=7, buildability_with_ai=8, buyer_clarity=7, willingness_to_pay=7). One strong validation conversation with a paying Data Cloud customer would push this to build.
